---
title: "Data Architecture"
---


## Overview of data sources

The data in the BPA Lab comes from three source systems: the process applications (multiple), the business process management system (BPMS) Camunda 8, and the FT-Factory, a physical model factory. The data is stored in two database management systems and can be grouped into data categories. 

Data in MySQL database management system:

Inside MySQL, two separate database schemas keep process application data apart from process execution data from the BPMS:

Application schema. This schema stores the data that the process applications create and use. It has three categories:
- Transactional data records business transactions, namely customer orders, production orders and purchasing orders.
- Stock data holds the inventory levels of component stock and product stock.
- Master data holds reference data that changes rarely, such as vendors.

BPMS schema. This schema stores the data that Camunda 8 produces while it runs process instances. Data can be logically differentiated into two categories:
- Event data records the execution history of process instances, for example of the logistics process, the purchasing process and other sub-processes. This data is the basis for process mining and process analytics.
- In addition, process variables, that process instances carry and change at runtime is available here.

Data in teh MongoDB database management system;

The FT-Factory (and other IOT devices) publishes data as messages through an MQTT broker. These messages are stored in the document-oriented database MongoDB, which suits the semi-structured, high-frequency nature of IoT data. These messsages contains among other aspects:
- Status data describes the current state of the factory, including station status, environmental status (for example sensor readings) and the overall factory production status.
- Stock data records the inventory of the factory’s high-bay warehouse.

## The MySQL data model

The following diagram shows the concrete data model of the MySQL database, including the entities and attributes of the current implementation:

![MySQL data model](images/mysql_data_model.png){#fig-mysql fig-align="center"}

The database serves as the central store for:

- **Product master data** — bicycle models and their components,
- **Customer data** and delivery addresses,
- **Stock levels** for components and finished goods,
- **Orders** — customer orders, production orders, purchase orders — together with their status history,
- **Vendor data**.

## Sample and master data

Documentation and sample data of the Fischertechnik factory are available in the [`Sample_data`](https://github.com/BpaLabTHCologne/bpa_lab_docs/tree/main/Sample_data) folder of the documentation repository. This data serves as:

- **initial master data** when setting up a new instance of the BPA Lab,
- **test data** for developing new components,
- a **demonstration baseline** for teaching sessions and presentations.

## Process data and the foundation for process mining

In addition to persistent master data, the running processes generate substantial amounts of **process data**:

- **Camunda 8** stores process instance data, variables, tokens, and lifecycle events.
- **MQTT messages** record the communication between job workers and controllers.
- **Job worker logs** capture technical operations and exceptions.

This event data is the foundation for **process mining** — a central teaching and demonstration component of the BPA Lab. Process mining allows students to:

- **discover** the actual flow of processes from event logs (and compare them to the modelled flow),
- **check conformance** between modelled and actual behaviour,
- **analyse performance** — durations, bottlenecks, rework loops.
